rationale: The four views consistently communicate two low, slender masses linked by a diagonal bridge, so the primary idea survives rotation. The split and folded geometry resonates with the references and avoids a primarily stepped silhouette. However, the masses remain visually shallow and somewhat fragmented, while the connector and several thin surface planes make the central relationship less exact than a clean two-mass composition. The void is present but reads more as a residual separation than a strongly defined public courtyard or undercroft.
warnings: The bridge appears to merge into multiple adjacent planes, weakening the precision of the split-mass reading.
The top view does not clearly establish a deliberate courtyard or major open-ground figure.
The low front elevation reduces the legibility of the main-versus-support hierarchy.
